title: Modbus device profile
description: Shape of a device profile. This schema validates structure and vocabulary only. It cannot check that a signal reference resolves, that an enum member exists, or that an expression parses -- see validate.py for that layer, and DECISIONS.md D1 for why expressions became load-bearing.

device.description: Which device and firmware this profile describes. One profile is one firmware version's register map, as in the company device library.

type.description: Device series identifier, as reported by the device_type register.

bitfields.description: Packed registers: a register whose bits are separate bool properties (D11). The register is not a property, but it is a named thing the register map documents, so it is declared once here and referenced by its bits. Its address is deliberately absent -- it is derived from the bits that reference it, which must all agree.

identifier.description: Also has to be a valid C identifier: the firmware X-macro pastes these into token names.

expression.description: Boolean expression over signal identifiers and enum member names. The reverse-dependency index is built by collecting signal identifiers out of these, so the grammar must stay small and total (DECISIONS.md D1). The grammar itself is not yet pinned down -- D3, open.

enum_member.description: Enum member name. Uppercase is allowed and often right -- acronyms like LPG read wrong lowercased, and C enum constants are conventionally uppercase. Must still be a valid C identifier for the X-macro. Member names are compared case-sensitively wherever expressions mention them.

value.description: A register value: an integer, a boolean, an enum member name, or a procedure parameter reference.

range.description: [min, max] in engineering units, after scale is applied.

enum_map.description: Raw register value -> member name. Mutually exclusive states.

access.description: Transport-level facts about what this device tolerates, as opposed to what Modbus permits.

binding.description: Where the value lives: an address space, an address in it, and how the value is packed there.

allOf.description: A coil or a discrete input IS a single bit, so the address already identifies it -- there is no bit index to give, and no other packing to choose.

then.description: A bool packed into a register needs to say which bit.

space.description: Which Modbus address space holds the value. These are separate address spaces, so the same address number in two of them is two different values.

encoding.description: How the value is packed into registers. This is a transport fact, not the value's type: the register span follows from the width (uint32 and float32 occupy two registers), and a scaled integer encoding carries a real.

count.description: Element count for arrays and strings. Omitted means 1. This is array length, not register span -- the span comes from the encoding width.

bit.description: Bit position within the register, for a bool packed into one.

wire_encoding.description: How a value is packed at its address. Which of these is legal depends on the property's semantic type, and validate.py holds that compatibility table: 'bit' carries a bool, an unsigned integer carries an enum, and a real travels either as a float or as a scaled integer. The address space is named separately by 'space' -- a coil and a discrete input are single bits by nature, so they take encoding 'bit'.

presentation.description: How a raw value becomes an engineering value. Shared by a signal and by each of its variants.

decimals.description: Decimal places to show. Display only -- scale already fixes the value.

display.description: How an int is rendered. 'version' means the raw bytes shown as hex and dot-joined with the leading zero trimmed, so 0x0130 reads as 1.30 -- which is 50 of the 55 bytewise decoders in the company library. Display only: the value is an integer.

allOf.description: type and the member map have to agree: an enum needs enum members, a flags value needs flag bits, and nothing else may carry either.
labels name a bool's two states, for display and for comparison in expressions. Only a bool has them.
A bitfield name only means something for a bool packed into a bit.
scale and decimals describe a continuous quantity; they are meaningless on anything else.
max_length belongs to text and only to text.
A command is invoked, so it is written and never read back as state.
A measurement is produced by the device: read-only, and a factory default is meaningless for it.
Presentation comes from exactly one place. If variants are given, the signal must not also carry a top-level interpretation -- otherwise there are two answers and no rule for which wins.
Only a bool is carried as a single bit, in any space.

binding.description: Where the value lives on the Modbus interface. OMITTED for an internal property: one that exists on the device but is not exposed on the bus (D8). Such a property is still generated into firmware's tables; it is simply absent from the register map, the documentation's map section, and anything a commissioning tool can reach.

kind.description: What sort of thing this is, which is what the generators switch on. 'setting' is persisted in non-volatile memory and has a factory default; 'measurement' is produced by the device and is volatile; 'command' is invoked and stores nothing. Explicit rather than inferred, because an internal property has no table or access pattern to infer it from.

type.description: What the value IS, independent of how any transport carries it. 'bool' is a truth value; 'int' a whole quantity; 'real' a continuous one; 'enum' one of named members; 'text' a character string. A set of independent bits is NOT a type: each bit is its own bool property bound to a bit of a register (D11). This is the type firmware should declare -- bool as bool, enum as an enum typedef -- and it is deliberately NOT the register width: a real may travel as float32 over two registers or as a scaled int16 over one, and a bool as a coil, a discrete input or a bit in a register.

storage.description: Width used when the value is persisted or held in a live-data struct. Omit it and the width is derived from range (and scale, for a real), which is the normal case; declare it only when the device stores the value wider than the range needs, or when there is no range to derive from. Checked against the range either way.

max_length.description: Maximum character count, for type 'text' only.

access.description: Access rights, following the company device library. Absent means read_write.

hidden.description: Service register: real, documented here, not shown to an ordinary user.

default.description: Factory default, in engineering units or as an enum member. Where the default depends on configuration, put it in constraints instead.

labels.description: Names for a bool's two states, e.g. { false: disabled, true: enabled }. What documentation and a commissioning tool show, and what an expression may compare against.

bitfield.description: The packed register in the top-level bitfields section that this bit belongs to. A reference rather than a repeated name, so the register's title and description are stated once and cannot disagree between bits.

variants.description: Alternative interpretations of the same register, one per configuration. A single variant is a modelling mistake: use top-level presentation instead.

constraints.description: Range/default/step that depend on configuration. First matching entry wins.

reread.description: What to re-read after writing this signal. The literal 'dependents' resolves against the derived reverse index; an explicit list covers registers the device re-clamps without any expression saying so.

danger.description: Drives how loudly the commissioning tool asks before running.

confirm.description: Shown verbatim before running. Says what breaks, not 'are you sure'.

duration_ms.description: Expected wall time, for progress UI.

enum_from.description: Take the allowed values from that signal's enum.
